name: icu
notes: Added 2026-10-03 for Web Tranche 1: JavaScriptCore/WTF require ICU >= 70.1 with the data, uc and i18n components (Source/cmake/OptionsJSCOnly.cmake, find_package(ICU 70.1 REQUIRED COMPONENTS data i18n uc)). It is a CRT port so the 06-web SDK does not depend on a host ICU (which would differ per OS and break the package boundary).

78.3 is the newest non-prerelease release (2026-03-17); 79.1rc is a release candidate. The archive's SHA-256 matches the digest GitHub publishes for the asset and its SHA-512 matches the release's signed SHASUM512.txt entry.

build.sysroot_stage=02-cxx and build.env.CRT_CXX_HOSTED=1: ICU is C++ and ships programs (icupkg, genrb, ...) with a plain `int main`; see porting/recipes/gperf.json for why both are needed. ICU is built without tests, samples and extras; ICU's runtime data is the default embedded data library (libicudata).
build.env.CRT_CXX_ENABLE_RTTI=1: ICU uses dynamic_cast/typeid (normalizer2.cpp, rbbi.cpp), and tools/crt-c++ compiles with -fno-rtti unless a port opts in.

Web Tranche 1 macOS replay (2026-10-04): build.target_overrides.macos.env.CRT_CXX_RUNTIME_LINKAGE=shared. ICU's own build runs the tools it just built (icupkg, genrb, pkgdata) against the shared libicuuc.dylib, which depends on @rpath/libc.dylib; a tool linked with the static runtime has no rpath to the CRT sysroot (and Apple's make/sh strip DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH under SIP), so dyld aborted with 'Library not loaded: @rpath/libc.dylib' while generating icudata.lst. Shared runtime linkage gives the tools the sysroot rpath and, as in Tranche 1B, one libc in the process.

Test changes for macOS (2026-10-04): the unicode tests pass -std=c++17 on macOS because Apple clang defaults to an older C++ dialect than ICU's headers need (std::is_same_v, auto template parameters), and the shared test now names libicu*.dylib per host like freetype.json/zlib.json instead of .so on every host.

macOS install names (2026-10-04): target_overrides.macos.configure_args --enable-rpath. ICU's Darwin makefile otherwise records a bare install name (libicuuc.78.dylib) that dyld cannot resolve without DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH (and a host-ABI audit cannot tell from a host library); --enable-rpath gives the absolute install-prefix name, the same convention as the sqlite amalgamation recipe, which the isolated-stage packaging rewrites to @rpath.

Windows/x64 (2026-10-05, Web Tranche 1 Windows replay): both recipe tests pass. build.target_overrides.windows: (1) --build=@CRT_MINGW_TRIPLE@ and the -U_WIN32/_WIN64/__MINGW32__/__MINGW64__ family in CFLAGS/CXXFLAGS/CPPFLAGS so ICU's platform.h picks its POSIX path (no windows.h exists in this sysroot), the recipe convention of curl/libpng; (2) env icu_cv_host_frag=mh-mingw64, because configure selects mh-mingw64 only if __MINGW64__ is defined at configure time and the -U above made it choose the 32-bit mh-mingw (a leading underscore on the embedded data symbol, icudt78_dat, so the static data library did not link, and a lib-prefixed data DLL that icuuc78.dll could not find); (3) make_args INVOKE/PKGDATA_INVOKE put PATH with ';' separators and the SDK bin directory (libc.dll) on the PATH of the tools ICU runs while building (icupkg, genrb, pkgdata; its own colon-separated value is not a Windows PATH, and the tools exit with STATUS_DLL_NOT_FOUND). The static libraries are named libsicu*.a (the data library is installed into bin/, not lib/), the import libraries libicu*.dll.a, the DLLs icu*78.dll. Three CRT/PAL defects were found and fixed by this port, none by patching ICU: the Windows startup kept at most 255 arguments and 8191 command-line characters and dropped the rest silently (ICU's 280-object libicuin link lost its libraries), a program named without .exe (`../bin/icupkg`) was not found by stat/access/spawn, and the port test environment lacked the SDK bin directory for DLLs built against libc.dll (tools/crt-port-build.py).
